notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; there is no hardware backend and no hardware run. The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but the upstream package is not installed and gymnasium/pygame are absent where the gate runs, so the fake backend is the package's own pure-Python reimplementation (fake.py), as in the Gymnasium exemplar. It was not compared with the upstream environment; the sim backend (gymnasium.make) was not run. Expected warnings are left: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset) and five G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, seed (reset and seed classes) and the two action arrays action.vR[*], action.vL[*]. Upstream states no physical unit for the wheel speeds (the play field is an abstract simulation plane) and the family bridge carries no unit for derived action arrays; no unit was invented. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings: every Fact cites a text line of the clone that shows it. The action bounds shown in REFERENCE.md are the environment's action space, derived by the bridge from the configured environment instance (the upstream default max_velocity and the fake's default), not a hand-written Limit; G4 treats such derived limits as upstream_code:PlanningMultiRobot-v0:action_space. The fake uses the upstream constructor defaults only as configuration; no fake start position or canned reply is quoted in a Fact or Limit. Only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. No operator-required limits and no site-limits overlay. NOT COVERED: rendering (cap.world.render.v1 is unbound; no frame is produced) and the info member predict_position, a Python callable dropped from the JSON state; the fidelity gaps say both. The full observation arrays are returned (5 robots, 19 non-target barriers), not a reduced stand-in.
